title: Patterns in Weather
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Patterns in Weather Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Weather is the condition of the air at a place and time: sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy, hot or cold. Weather can be observed, recorded and described, and it shows patterns such as the dry and rainy seasons. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 3, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): kinds of weather, weather tools, recording weather, weather and safety, and weather patterns. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather tells us what the air is like outside: it can be sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy or stormy, and hot or cool. We use a thermometer to measure temperature and a rain gauge to measure rain.

When we record the weather every day, we see patterns: in the Philippines, the dry season has many sunny days and the rainy season has many rainy afternoons. Knowing the weather helps us choose what to wear and stay safe.

Example

Which tool measures rain?

It collects water.

Answer: a rain gauge

Example

Dark clouds and strong wind. What might come?

Think of a storm.

Answer: rain or a thunderstorm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the weather is the same every day.
  • Standing under a tree during lightning.
  • Thinking clouds are made of smoke.

items.e: Changes in pressure help forecast weather.

items.q: Why should you bring an umbrella when the forecast says rain?

items.q: Which of these describes cloudy weather?
c: The grass is white and crunchy in the cold morning.
The sky is gray and covered in clouds, but it is dry.
Trees sway and kites fly well.
The sun is shining and the sky is blue.
items.e: Look and listen to describe the weather.

items.q: Which weather is best for drying clothes outside?
items.e: Heat and wind help water evaporate.

items.q: Which agency tells us the weather forecast in the Philippines?

items.q: What forms clouds?
c: tiny water droplets made when water vapor cools in the air
items.e: Water vapor condenses into droplets.

items.q: What is an air mass?
c: a huge body of air with about the same temperature and humidity throughout
items.e: Air masses can cover thousands of kilometers.

items.q: Which tool measures the amount of rain that falls?
items.e: It collects rainwater so it can be measured.

items.q: Why do cold fronts often bring thunderstorms?
c: Warm, moist air is pushed up quickly, cools and forms tall clouds.
items.e: Fast-rising air builds storm clouds.

items.q: What causes air masses to move?
c: winds and differences in air pressure
items.e: Air moves from high to low pressure.
